Necrosis in this mouse is driven at least partly by coronary vascular smooth muscle dysfunction, which a vasodilator prevents; CMD1L patients had normal coronary arteries and no ischemia.

evidence.reference_title: Prevention of cardiomyopathy in delta-sarcoglycan knockout mice after systemic transfer of targeted adeno-associated viral vectors.
evidence.snippet: Left ventricular function remained stable in mice expressing Sgcd while it deteriorated in EGFP controls within 6 months, paralleled by increased expression of brain natriuretic peptide, a molecular marker of heart failure.

evidence.reference_title: Rescue of hereditary form of dilated cardiomyopathy by rAAV-mediated somatic gene therapy: amelioration of morphological findings, sarcolemmal permeability, cardiac performances, and the prognosis of TO-2 hamsters.
evidence.snippet: The transgene preserved sarcolemmal permeability detected in situ by mutual exclusivity between cardiomyocytes taking up intravenously administered Evans blue dye and expressing the delta-SG transgene throughout life.

nodes.description: Cardiac overexpression of the founding human allele produces young-onset DCM with increased lethality, nuclear retention of delta-sarcoglycan, and mislocalized lamin A/C and emerin.

Loss of cardiomyocytes is the step proposed to precede replacement fibrosis and ventricular remodeling. Focal myocardial necrosis is the histological hallmark in Sgcd-null mice, a recessive model. In CMD1L the only tissue is one explanted S151A-family heart, which showed myocyte hypertrophy and moderate fibrosis without ischemia; myocyte loss itself was not described in it.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of the sarcoglycan-sarcospan complex in vascular smooth muscle: a novel mechanism for cardiomyopathy and muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: We found that only Sgcd null mice developed cardiomyopathy with focal areas of necrosis as the histological hallmark in cardiac and skeletal muscle.

nodes.description: Myocyte hypertrophy in the one explanted S151A-family heart.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the human delta-sarcoglycan gene in familial and sporadic dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Gross and histopathologic examination of the explanted heart demonstrated features of classic DCM, including increased heart weight, left ventricular dilatation, histopathologic evidence of myocyte hypertrophy, and moderate fibrosis.

nodes.description: Inbred hypertrophic (BIO14.6) and dilated (TO-2) sublines share a deletion that abolishes delta-sarcoglycan. Cardiomyopathy and muscular dystrophy are inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. AAV delta-sarcoglycan restores sarcolemmal integrity and prolongs survival in TO-2.
Symptomatic heart failure at a young age in all affected members of the S151A family.

nodes.description: The defining feature. It was present in all affected S151A-family members and in the two sporadic p.Lys238del children, and was full-blown in one of two R71T carriers. Too few patients are reported to estimate a frequency.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the human delta-sarcoglycan gene in familial and sporadic dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Echocardiographically, all affected individuals had severely dilated left ventricular chambers (with Z scores > 4) and moderate to severe systolic dysfunction (ejection fractions < 35%).

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation, Arg71Thr, in the delta-sarcoglycan gene is associated with dilated cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: One of the mutation carriers fulfills diagnostic criteria for DCM and is also symptomatic. The other mutation carrier has slightly dilated left ventricle and well preserved systolic function.

nodes.description: The proposed molecular effect is interference by the mutant protein with the sarcoglycan-sarcospan subcomplex of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex. The two experimental systems disagree on how this happens. In rat cardiomyocytes, R97Q and R71T traffic normally and the complex assembles, but the membrane is fragile under strain. In transgenic mice, S151A is retained in the nucleus and sequesters beta- and gamma-sarcoglycan. Both systems overexpress the mutant, and R97Q was called a polymorphism in the founding report. In the one p.Lys238del explant, delta-sarcoglycan staining was reduced while alpha-, beta-, gamma-sarcoglycan and dystrophin staining was preserved.

evidence.reference_title: Dilated cardiomyopathy mutations in δ-sarcoglycan exert a dominant-negative effect on cardiac myocyte mechanical stability.
evidence.snippet: This study demonstrates that DCM mutant δ-sarcoglycans can be stably expressed in adult rat cardiac myocytes and traffic similarly to wild-type δ-sarcoglycan to the plasma membrane, without perturbing assembly of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex.

evidence.reference_title: Dilated cardiomyopathy mutations in δ-sarcoglycan exert a dominant-negative effect on cardiac myocyte mechanical stability.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, the R71T mutation creates an ectopic N-linked glycosylation site that results in aberrant glycosylation of the extracellular domain of δ-sarcoglycan.

nodes.description: The founding allele at native dosage gave only increased heart-to-body weight at one year, with preserved echocardiographic function and no histopathology. Crossing heterozygotes produced no homozygous S151A offspring, suggesting embryonic lethality of the homozygous genotype.

nodes.description: The proposed initiating lesion is a single germline SGCD missense or in-frame variant (S151A, p.Lys238del, R71T), plus one canonical splice variant. Delta-sarcoglycan is a sarcolemmal transmembrane glycoprotein of striated and smooth muscle that helps stabilize the sarcolemma. The causal status of every reported allele is uncertain: ClinGen rates the gene-disease relationship Limited, and the founding S151A allele was not associated with cardiac disease in an independent family.

evidence.snippet: Mutations affecting the secondary structure were identified in one family and two sporadic cases, whereas immunofluorescence analysis of myocardium from one of these patients demonstrated significant reduction in delta-sarcoglycan staining.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a novel sarcoglycan gene at 5q33 encoding a sarcolemmal 35 kDa glycoprotein.
evidence.snippet: Its mRNA expression is abundant in striated and smooth muscles, with a main 8 kb transcript, encoding a predicted basic transmembrane glycoprotein of 290 amino acids.

evidence.reference_title: Both hypertrophic and dilated cardiomyopathies are caused by mutation of the same gene, delta-sarcoglycan, in hamster: an animal model of disrupted dystrophin-associated glycoprotein complex.
evidence.snippet: We elucidated the molecular interaction of dystrophin-associated glycoproteins including delta-SG, by using an in vitro pull-down study and ligand overlay assay, which indicates the functional role of delta-SG in stabilizing sarcolemma.

evidence.reference_title: Does delta-sarcoglycan-associated autosomal-dominant cardiomyopathy exist?
evidence.snippet: Our findings demonstrate that, even in the presence of a second disease-causing mutation, the p.S151A mutation in the delta-sarcoglycan gene does not result in cardiomyopathy.

genetic_context.description: The dominant-negative category is the authors' proposal, supported only by overexpression systems. Haploinsufficiency is not supported, because heterozygous relatives of LGMD2F patients have not been described as affected.

nodes.description: Loss of delta-sarcoglycan reduces the other sarcoglycans and causes systolic dysfunction, myocardial degeneration and sudden death.

Complete delta-sarcoglycan loss causes cardiomyopathy with focal necrosis and muscular dystrophy, together with vascular smooth muscle sarcoglycan loss and coronary irregularities. It models the recessive null state, not a heterozygous dominant allele.

Cardiomyocytes expressing mutant delta-sarcoglycan take up membrane-impermeant dye and develop contractures under cyclic stretch. This parallels the sarcolemmal instability that complete delta-sarcoglycan loss causes. It has not been measured in patient tissue or in patient-derived cardiomyocytes.
